posts.title: Yoga Is Yoga
posts.hook: Where I sweat in New York, free to really expensive, and the one studio I'm not about.

posts.title: Admitting Flaws Only Works If You're Good
posts.hook: "Be vulnerable" is the most overrated sales advice online. A 1962 car rental ad and one spilled coffee explain why.

posts.title: Your Dream Home Won't Fix Your Brain
posts.hook: A high ceiling only changes how you think if you actually look up.

posts.title: Your Yoga Class Is Basically a Gym
posts.hook: The ancient part of yoga is the five minutes you skip to beat traffic.

posts.title: Grand Gestures Are for Bad Partners
posts.hook: The couples who last don't do big romance. They answer "look at this bird.”

posts.title: Being Anti-AI Is Smarter Than You Think
posts.hook: The AI fight isn't about robots. It's about who gets paid when the machine does the work.

posts.title: The Banana Peel Is the Material
posts.hook: Yahvi Duggal weaves cloth out of what kitchens throw away. You can't mass-produce a look that depends on what got cooked yesterday.

posts.title: The Painting Isn't Finished Until You Walk Up
posts.hook: Casey Wakefield paints abstracts in Gilbert, Arizona. Her new show is about the one thing no painter controls: what you bring with you.

posts.title: Same Marketing. Different Tags.
posts.hook: Abercrombie's women's "Wool-Blend" cardigan is $120 and 6% wool. The men's merino cardigan is $95 and 100% wool. We pay more for less, and I think the name is doing the heavy lifting.

posts.title: The Gray Floor Problem
posts.hook: Why are we all trying to be influencers of the same things? Our feeds, our cafés, and our houses are turning into one look, and the reason isn't bad taste.

posts.title: Don't Sand Yourself Down
posts.hook: AI can now write the expert thread, the clean carousel, and the polished bio. That makes the strange, specific, opinionated parts of you the only things left that nobody can copy.

posts.title: Everyone You Meet Is You
posts.hook: I've believed Andy Weir's "The Egg" since 2022. It made me kinder, it took away my fear of dying, and it ruined the idea of "strangers" for me in the best way.

posts.title: The Chatbot That Scared Its Maker
posts.hook: In the 1960s, a simple program made people feel understood. Its inventor spent the rest of his life warning us about what that meant.
